rules.title: static mut access requires unsafe
rules.statement: Reading or place-assigning a `static mut` item requires an enclosing `unsafe` block.

rules.title: static items addressed as places
rules.statement: Every `static [mut]` item has link symbol `<pkg>$<NAME>` (extern-block-declared statics keep the bare name); reads lower as a dereference of the static's address (`Deref(VarRef("__static_addr:<sym>", *T))`) and writes lower as a store through the same address expression.

rules.title: Local/param binding shadows a module static
rules.statement: A module static name is treated as a static reference only when not shadowed by an in-scope local binding or a type/const-generic parameter of the same name.

rules.title: Union field write is safe, read is unsafe
rules.statement: Writing a union field is safe and does not require `unsafe`; only reading a union field requires an enclosing `unsafe` block. A transient write-lhs flag, set before lowering a place-assign's LHS and RAII-restored after, tells field-read lowering to skip the union-read unsafe gate for that write.

rules.title: Tuple-struct fields named by ordinal
rules.statement: Tuple-struct fields are named by their zero-based positional index rendered as a decimal string ("0", "1", ...); the backing strings are pool-allocated so string_view field names stay valid for the struct registry's lifetime.

rules.title: Generic compile-time const re-resolved per instantiation
rules.statement: A generic compile-time const `const X<T1,...>: WritStatic = @{ ... };` re-resolves its value-AST under each use-site's bound type-args: `<type:Ti>` slots resolve to the concrete type and the resulting value has a distinct per-instantiation identity (via an FNV hash of the AST walk substituting each type-var name for the concrete type's string form).
rules.uncertainty: Writ-static metaprogramming feature; identity-per-instantiation inferred from comment.

rules.title: Trait-qualified method mangling on name collision
rules.statement: When two distinct traits define a same-named method with the same signature on one type, the colliding methods re-key under `<target>__<trait>__<method>`; a plain base `<target>__<method>` with more than one such entry is ambiguous for concrete-receiver dispatch and requires disambiguation.

rules.title: Multiple impls of one trait at distinct args coexist
rules.statement: Multiple impls of the same trait name for one Self type at distinct concrete trait type-args (e.g. `From<i8> for i32` and `From<i16> for i32`, or a concrete `Iterator<i32>` vs a generic `Iterator<&T> for VecIter<T>`) are distinct impls: an all-impls registry (keyed same as the single-valued impl registry) retains every one so a parametrized bound `T: Trait<Args>` can be checked against actual trait-args; coherence/duplicate-detection keys separately on `Trait[arg1,...]::Target`; methods are mangled with the impl's concrete trait type-args so they coexist.

rules.title: Trait objects require object-safe traits
rules.statement: A trait used as a trait object (`&dyn`/`*dyn`/`Box<dyn>`) must be object-safe (dyn-compatible, Rust E0038); a non-object-safe trait used this way is an error, checked when the `dyn Trait` type is resolved and reported once per offending trait.

rules.title: Name resolution order: current package, imports, bare
rules.statement: An unqualified struct/datatype/enum/trait name resolves by trying the current package's qualified key, then each imported package (and its transitive `pub use` re-exports), then the bare (legacy/unqualified) key.

rules.title: Transitive pub-use re-export resolution
rules.statement: Resolving a name in the context of imported packages searches each imported package plus, transitively and cycle-safely, all packages reachable through their `pub use` re-exports.

rules.title: Cross-package items checked even via bare key
rules.statement: An item resolved through the bare/unqualified key is subject to the same pub-access check as a package-qualified hit when it belongs to a package different from the current one; only own-package bare entries (primitives/builtins) bypass the check.

rules.title: use pkg from module restricts type/enum/trait visibility
rules.statement: `use pkg from <module>;` restricts the package's types, enums, and traits (not only its free functions) to the named owning module; a candidate whose package is owned by a different module than the one specified is skipped during resolution.

rules.title: Const-generic parameters bind as const-vars
rules.statement: A const-generic type parameter `const N: T` binds in scope as a ConstVar carrying its declared const type; a non-const type parameter binds as a type variable.

rules.title: Type/const params shadow outer same-named params
rules.statement: Pushing a scope of type parameters shadows any outer binding of the same name (type, bounds, and `?Sized` relaxation), and popping restores the prior binding exactly; this permits e.g. a method `<T>` to shadow an enclosing trait/impl `<T>`.

rules.title: Only ?Sized is a permitted relaxed bound
rules.statement: A relaxed bound (`?Trait`) is permitted only for `Sized`; any other relaxed bound is an error. Seeing `?Sized` clears the parameter's implicit `Sized` requirement, and the relaxed entry is removed from the bounds list so downstream code sees only positive bounds.

rules.title: ?Sized param substituted where Sized required errors
rules.statement: When a type parameter carrying `?Sized` is passed as a type-argument to a callee whose corresponding parameter requires `Sized`, the same unsized-substitution diagnostic is emitted as for an explicit unsized substitution.

rules.title: Associated-type equality clauses must hold
rules.statement: A bound `Trait<Assoc = Type>` holds for a concrete type only if each expected associated type equals the impl's actual `type Assoc = ...` resolution after substitution.

rules.title: Bare identifier pattern naming a module const matches by value
rules.statement: In `match scrutinee { NAME => ... }`, if `NAME` names a module-level `const`, the arm's pattern is evaluated (ctfe) against the const's retained initializer AST and lowered as a value pattern (int/bool/char), rather than binding the scrutinee to a fresh local named `NAME`.

rules.title: Type alias may declare type and lifetime parameters
rules.statement: A `type` alias declaration may carry its own generic type parameters and lifetime parameters (e.g. `type Foo<'z, T> = ...;`); a non-generic alias has an empty type-params list.

rules.title: Struct/enum variance computed by field-type fixpoint
rules.statement: Variance of each struct/enum's type and lifetime parameters is computed by a fixed-point iteration over its fields' types, and recorded per declaration (keyed `pkg.Name`) as a map from parameter index (`#i` for type params, `@i` for lifetime params) to variance.
rules.uncertainty: Only the declaration and summary comment are in this slice; the fixed-point algorithm itself is defined elsewhere.

rules.title: Declared lifetime outlives bounds 'long: 'short
rules.statement: A `'long: 'short` outlives clause may appear in a fn/struct/enum/impl generic header or `where` clause; sema reads these as (long, short) lifetime-name pairs from `LIFETIME_PARAM` items carrying a non-empty bound list.

rules.title: Associated type definitions carry independent GAT params
rules.statement: An associated-type implementation (`type Item<T> = ...` inside an `impl`) records its own generic type parameters (from the GAT declaration) separately from the enclosing impl's type parameters; both parameter lists are retained for substitution at each projection use-site.

rules.title: Self::Item resolves through the impl's trait before impl registration
rules.statement: Inside a trait definition, `Self::Item` resolves via the trait currently being defined; inside an impl's method signatures during signature collection, `Self::Item<X>` resolves via the impl's trait even though the impl itself is not yet present in the impl registry at that point.

rules.title: Method-call dispatch falls back to blanket impls
rules.statement: A blanket impl `impl<T: Bound1 [+ Bound2...]> Trait for T { ... }` is consulted for method-call resolution when direct lookup on the concrete receiver type fails; it matches only if the receiver satisfies the primary bound AND every extra bound (AND-filter across all bounds), and, per associated-type-equality clauses declared on each bound, only if those associated-type equalities also hold for the receiver.

rules.title: pub(module) items are module-private across module boundaries
rules.statement: A type/enum/trait/struct marked module-only-public, resolved through an imported package, is checked against the accessing site's owning module: if the item's owning module differs from the accessing module, resolution reports a module-private diagnostic even though the item is otherwise `pub`.

rules.title: Trait name lookup does not enforce pub-visibility
rules.statement: Resolving a trait name does not run the pub-access check that struct/datatype/enum lookup runs; a private/foreign trait name still resolves at general reference sites (bound checks, fallback probes). Visibility for a foreign trait is instead enforced explicitly at the site that introduces it into an impl.
rules.uncertainty: The enforcement site (collect_impl) is outside this slice; only the deferral is directly observed here.

rules.title: Struct representation queries bypass privacy
rules.statement: A struct lookup performed to answer a layout/representation question (e.g. an internal representation check consulted during monomorphization from a foreign package's context) uses a pub-check-free accessor, distinct from the pub-checked name-resolution accessor; visibility is not enforced for representation-only queries.
